## TRA Timeline

#### Up-C de-SPAC and TRA execution

- 2016-07-05: Form-of TRA filed as Exhibit 10.4 to the merger-signing 8-K with Gores Holdings
- 2016-11-04: Executed TRA dated as of de-SPAC close, 85% of cash tax savings to Apollo and Metropoulos beneficiary blocks
- 2016-11-09: De-SPAC closing 8-K attaches the executed TRA as Exhibit 10.15

#### Apollo buyout (amendment)

- 2017-04-10: Between-Holders Letter Agreement reassigns 5 percentage points of AP Hostess's Participation Percentage to the CDM block pro rata (not filed as exhibit; referenced in later recitals)
- 2018-01-26: Buyout and Amendment Agreement: Apollo exits the TRA for $34M cash plus contingent $10M CoC payment if a definitive CoC agreement signed within one year (window expired without trigger); CDM block remains

#### Smucker acquisition (silent on TRA)

- 2023-09-10: Smucker merger agreement signed; the merger agreement and signing 8-K contain no TRA references
- 2023-11-07: Smucker merger closes; Hostess Brands continues as a wholly-owned Smucker subsidiary; closing 8-K does not reference the TRA; no Item 1.02 termination filed; Hostess deregisters

## Explanation

Hostess Brands executed its Tax Receivable Agreement at the November 2016 de-SPAC combination with Gores Holdings, paying 85% of the cash tax savings on Section 754 basis step-ups (from exchanges of Hostess Holdings Class B Units), pre-IPO Hostess Holdings tax attributes, and imputed interest to the Apollo block (AP Hostess Holdings, L.P.) and the Metropoulos block (Hostess CDM Co-Invest series, CDM Hostess Class C series, and C. Dean Metropoulos individually). In January 2018, Apollo exited the TRA via a $34M buyout amendment with a contingent $10M change-of-control payment that never triggered; the contract continued in force for the CDM block only. The November 2023 Smucker acquisition was structured silently with respect to the TRA: no termination amendment, no Item 1.02 filing, no closing-8-K reference, and the TRA legal obligor (Hostess Brands, Inc.) survived as a wholly-owned Smucker subsidiary. The TRA may continue as an assumed obligation or have been quietly settled post-close; Hostess deregistered so its fate is not visible under the Hostess CIK and tracking requires Smucker's filings. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
